extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent agents/attorneys, and USPTO staff handling patent term extensions
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedures for preparing, filing, prosecuting, and calculating patent term extensions under 35 U.S.C. 156 (including timing, required contents, duties of disclosure, interim extensions, withdrawal, and product-specific calculation methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for extension of patent term (§ 1.720)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent may be extended if the patent and application satisfy specified conditions listed in paragraphs (a) through (h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions enumerated: (a) the patent claims a product or a method of using or manufacturing a product as defined in § 1.710; (b) the term of the patent has never been previously extended (except for extensions pursuant to §§ 1.701, 1.760, or 1.790); (c) an application for extension is submitted in compliance with § 1.740; (d) the product has been subject to a regulatory review period as defined in 35 U.S.C. 156(g) before commercial marketing/use; (e) the product has received permission for commercial marketing or use and (1) that permission is the first received permission for commercial marketing/use under the provision of law under which the applicable regulatory review occurred, or (2) for patents (other than certain recombinant DNA manufacturing claims), the permission is the first permitted commercial marketing/use of a product manufactured under the process claimed, or (3) special rule for new animal drugs or veterinary biological products addressing food-producing vs non-food-producing animals; (f) the application is submitted within the sixty-day period beginning on the date the product first received permission for commercial marketing/use (with special-case timing language for recombinant-DNA manufacturing claims and certain animal drug situations); (g) the patent term, including any interim extension under § 1.790, has not expired before submission in compliance with § 1.741; and (h) no other patent term has been extended for the same regulatory review period for the product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant and signature requirements (§ 1.730)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who may submit an application for extension and signature rules for the application filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any application must be submitted by the owner of record of the patent or its agent and must comply with § 1.740. If submitted by the patent owner, the application must be signed either by (1) the patent owner in compliance with § 3.73(c) or (2) a registered practitioner on behalf of the patent owner. If submitted on behalf of the owner by an agent (e.g., licensee), it must be signed by a registered practitioner on behalf of the agent. The Office may require proof that the agent or practitioner is authorized to act on behalf of the patent owner or agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application written content and required items (§ 1.740 general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal application for extension must be made in writing to the Director and include a comprehensive set of required items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal application must include the items enumerated in paragraphs (a)(1) through (a)(15). The application must be in writing to the Director and include identification of the approved product, identification of the Federal statute and provision under which regulatory review occurred, identification of the date product received permission for commercial marketing/use, and other required content described below (see entries for the specific items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the approved product, statute, and approval date (§ 1.740(a)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must provide a complete identification of the approved product, the Federal statute (and applicable provision) under which regulatory review occurred, and the date the product received permission for commercial marketing/use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification should be by appropriate chemical and generic name, physical structure or characteristics (for the product); the exact Federal statute and applicable provision of law; and the specific date the product received permission for commercial marketing/use under that provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug-specific active ingredient disclosure (§ 1.740(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: For drug products, identify each active ingredient and state prior approval history for each active ingredient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each active ingredient in a drug product, include identification and either a statement that it has not been previously approved for commercial marketing/use under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the Public Health Service Act, or the Virus-Serum-Toxin Act, or provide the date the active ingredient was approved (alone or in combination), the use for which it was approved, and the provision of law under which it was approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of timely submission (60‑day statement) (§ 1.740(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must state that the application is being submitted within the sixty-day period permitted under § 1.720(f) and identify the date of the last day on which the application could be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear statement must begin on a new page indicating that the filing is within the statutory 60‑day window and specifying the last eligible filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent identification and documentary attachments (§ 1.740(a)(6)-(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide complete identification of the patent and copies of the patent and any post‑grant instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include inventor name(s), patent number, date of issue, date of expiration; a copy of the patent including the entire specification (including claims) and drawings; and copies of any disclaimer, certificate of correction, receipt of maintenance fee payment, or reexamination certificate issued in the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement that patent claims the approved product and claim‑by‑claim showing (§ 1.740(a)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement and showing that the patent claims the approved product or a method of using/manufacturing it, listing each applicable claim and demonstrating how at least one such claim reads on the product/method/manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The showing must list each applicable patent claim and explicitly demonstrate the manner in which at least one such patent claim reads on: (i) the approved product (if there are product claims); (ii) the method of using the approved product (if there are method-of-use claims); and (iii) the method of manufacturing the approved product (if there are manufacturing-method claims). This showing must appear in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant regulatory dates under 35 U.S.C. 156(g) (product‑type specific) (§ 1.740(a)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the relevant dates and information required by 35 U.S.C. 156(g) so the Secretary of HHS or Agriculture can determine the applicable regulatory review period; the specific dates required depend on product type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin on a new page and provide the dates and information for the product type: For human drugs/biologicals: IND effective date and number, NDA/PLA submission date and number, date of approval; for new animal drugs: major health/environmental test initiation date or effective exemption date, NADA submission date and number, NADA approval date; for veterinary biological products: effective date authority to prepare experimental product, license application submission date, license issue date; for food or color additives: date major health/environmental test initiated, date petition or product development protocol submitted, and dates of approval or Federal Register actions; for medical devices: IDE effective date/IDE number or first clinical investigation date and substantiation, initial submission/approval dates under section 515 or product development protocol dates. Provide any substantiation documents as available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of marketing applicant's significant activities during regulatory review (§ 1.740(a)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief description of significant activities undertaken by the marketing applicant during the applicable regulatory review period and the significant dates applicable to such activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This must begin on a new page and summarize the marketing applicant's substantive efforts and milestone dates during the regulatory review period to assist in determining the regulatory review period and entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's opinion of eligibility and claimed extension length (§ 1.740(a)(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement by the applicant that, in the applicant's opinion, the patent is eligible for extension and the length of extension claimed, including how the length was determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin on a new page and include a calculation or explanation of how the applicant computed the claimed extension length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of duty to disclose (reference to § 1.765) (§ 1.740(a)(13))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must state acknowledgment of a duty to disclose to the USPTO Director and the appropriate Secretary any information material to entitlement determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit acknowledgement that duty of disclosure exists and references § 1.765; failure to disclose material information can preclude extension (see § 1.765).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee and contact information (§ 1.740(a)(14)-(15))
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the prescribed fee for receiving/acting upon the application and contact information for correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide payment of prescribed fee per § 1.20(j) and include name, address, telephone number, and email address of the person to whom inquiries and correspondence related to the application are to be directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing and correction of informalities (§ 1.740(b)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications (and related submissions) must be submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system and the Office will notify/applicant may correct informality within two months if the application is informal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must comply with USPTO electronic filing system requirements. If the Office deems an application informal, it will notify the applicant and the applicant has two months (or other time set in the notice) to correct the informality; the time may be extended under § 1.136 unless the notice says otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application filing date and minimum elements (§ 1.741(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'complete application' receives a filing date only when certain minimum elements are included; these minimum elements are required to establish a filing date and trigger timing rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing date is the date a complete application is received via the USPTO electronic filing system or pursuant to § 1.8(a)(1)(i)(C) and (a)(1)(ii). A complete application must include: (1) identification of the approved product; (2) identification of each Federal statute under which regulatory review occurred; (3) identification of the patent for which extension is sought; (4) identification of each claim of the patent which claims the approved product or a method of using or manufacturing it; and (5) sufficient information to enable the Director to determine under subsections (a) and (b) of 35 U.S.C. 156 the eligibility of a patent for extension. If incomplete, the Office will notify the applicant and petition procedures and fees apply for review of completeness/filing date determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition procedure for incomplete applications (§ 1.741(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office finds an application incomplete or sets a filing date the applicant disputes, a petition with fee must be filed within two months of the mail date of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be filed pursuant to the paragraph and accompanied by the fee in § 1.17(f) within two months of the mail date of the notice that the application is incomplete or the notice according the filing date complained of. Time may be extended under § 1.136 unless the notice states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of eligibility and notice; reconsideration (§ 1.750)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director (or delegated officials) may determine eligibility for extension based on application representations, may request additional inquiries, and will mail a notice constituting final determination; limited reconsideration is permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination may be made solely on the basis of representations in the application and may be delegated. The Director or other officials may require further independent inquiries. The Office will mail a notice to applicant containing the determination of eligibility and any period of extension; this notice constitutes the final determination. A single request for reconsideration of a final determination may be made if filed by the applicant within the time set in the notice or, if no time is set, within one month from the date of final determination. Time periods are subject to § 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extension procedures (§ 1.760)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for requesting and granting interim extensions pending final determination on a formal application filed in compliance with § 1.740.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant with a formal application may request one or more interim extensions for periods up to one year each pending final determination; such request should be filed at least three months prior to patent expiration. The Director may issue interim extensions without a request for up to one year each until final determination. Patent owner or agent will be notified when an interim extension is granted and notice will be published in the Official Gazette. Interim extensions will be recorded in the patent file and considered part of the original patent. Interim extensions will not exceed the maximum period for which the applicant would be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure in patent term extension proceedings (§ 1.765)
rubrics_metrics.description: A duty of candor and good faith exists on patent owners, their representatives, and any individuals substantively involved in the proceeding to disclose material adverse information to the Office and the appropriate Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those identified (owner/agent, each attorney or agent who represents the patent owner, and every other individual substantively involved) must disclose material information adverse to entitlement as soon as practical after becoming aware. 'Material' means there is a substantial likelihood the Office or Secretary would consider it important in determinations. Disclosures must be accompanied by copies of each written document disclosed and made to the Office or Secretary as appropriate (duplicate certified copies if material to both). Disclosures may be made through an attorney/agent or the patent owner acting pro se; disclosure to such attorney/agent satisfies the duty for other individuals. Such attorney/agent has no duty to transmit information not material to entitlement. No extension will be issued if fraud on the Office or Secretary was practiced/attempted or duty of disclosure was violated through bad faith or gross negligence; if established by clear and convincing evidence, a final determination will be made pursuant to § 1.750 that the patent is not eligible. Duty rests on the identified individuals and submissions by third parties (protests or otherwise) will not be considered by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express withdrawal of application (§ 1.770)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may expressly withdraw an extension application before final determination subject to signature and timing rules; withdrawal does not entitle fee refund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express withdrawal must be by written declaration filed in the Office and signed by the owner of record or its agent. An application may not be expressly withdrawn after the date permitted for reply to the application. A withdrawal is effective when acknowledged in writing by the Office. Filing and acceptance of an express withdrawal does not entitle applicant to a refund of the filing fee (§ 1.20(j)) or any portion thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of patent term extension for human drugs/antibiotics/human biological products (§ 1.775)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for computing extension length in days for human drugs, antibiotic drugs, and human biological products, including how the regulatory review period is measured and reductions applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If eligible, the patent term is extended by the number of days calculated per this section and runs from the original expiration date (or earlier terminal disclaimer date). The extension equals the length of the regulatory review period as determined by HHS, reduced as appropriate under paragraphs (d)(1)-(d)(6). The regulatory review period under 35 U.S.C. 156(g)(1)(B) is the sum of: (c)(1) days from the date an exemption under section 505(i) or 507(d) became effective for the approved product to the date the application was initially submitted under those sections or section 351 of PHSA; and (c)(2) days from initial submission under section 351 or section 505(b) or section 507 to the date such application was approved. Reductions per (d) include subtracting days of the periods that were on/before the patent issue date, subtracting days during which HHS determines applicant did not act with due diligence, subtracting one-half the remaining days of (c)(1) (ignoring half days), then adding the resulting days to the original patent term shortened by any terminal disclaimer. Alternative computations include adding 14 years to approval date or adding 5 years to original expiration (depending on issue date) and selecting earlier dates per the multi-step comparison rules in paragraphs (d)(2)-(d)(6). The full section lists the precise subtraction, addition, and comparison steps and special rules for patents issued before/after Sept. 24, 1984 and for certain pre‑1984 submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of patent term extension for food additives and color additives (§ 1.776)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for computing extension for food or color additives: definition of regulatory review period and reductions/additive comparisons analogous to human drug rules but using dates relevant to petitions/regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extension equals the regulatory review period as determined by HHS under 35 U.S.C. 156(g)(2)(B), reduced per paragraphs (d)(1)-(d)(6). The regulatory review period is the sum of (c)(1) days from initiation of a major health/environmental effects test to initial petition submission and (c)(2) days from petition submission to the date the regulation became effective (or resolved after objections, or final proceedings permitting commercial marketing). Reductions include subtracting days on/before patent issue, subtracting days where applicant did not act with due diligence, subtracting one-half the remaining days of (c)(1), adding the resulting days to the original term shortened by any terminal disclaimer, adding 14 years to regulation effective date (or resolved date) and comparing computed dates, then applying additional 5-year/2-year addbacks and comparisons for patents issued after/before Sept. 24, 1984 and for petitions/submissions before that date as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of patent term extension for medical devices (§ 1.777)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for computing extension for medical devices: definition of regulatory review period using clinical investigation/IDE/section 515 submission dates and analogous reduction/comparison rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory review period under 35 U.S.C. 156(g)(3)(B) is the sum of (c)(1) days from the date a clinical investigation on humans involving the device began to the date an application was initially submitted under section 515, and (c)(2) days from the initial section 515 submission to the date such application was approved (or from notice of completion of a product development protocol to protocol completion). Reductions and calculation steps mirror the patterns in § 1.775: subtract days on/before patent issue, subtract days of lack of due diligence, subtract one-half the remaining days of (c)(1), add to original term shortened by terminal disclaimer, add 14 years to approval or protocol completion date, compare computed dates and select earlier, and apply 5-year/2-year adjustments for patents issued after/before Sept. 24, 1984 with special-case triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of patent term extension for animal drugs (§ 1.778)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for computing extension for animal drugs: definition of regulatory review period using major health/environmental test initiation or exemption dates and NADA submission/approval dates, with reductions and comparisons analogous to other product-specific rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 35 U.S.C. 156(g)(4)(B), the regulatory review period is the sum of: (c)(1) number of days beginning on the earlier of a major health/environmental effects test initiation or the date an exemption under section 512(j) became effective and ending on the date an application was initially submitted under section 512; and (c)(2) number of days from initial submission under subsection (b) of section 512 to the date of approval. Reductions include subtracting days on/before patent issue, subtracting days during which HHS determines lack of due diligence, and subtracting one-half of the remaining days per the pattern; other steps mirror the computational/comparison framework used for human drugs, foods, and devices as set forth in the section.
